source_refs.note: Exercise 3.5, Question 5: prove the x <-> 1 - x symmetry on [0, 1] and evaluate; book p. 102. Key on p. 300 under 'Exercise 3.2'.

blocks.prompt: 5 Prove that \(\int_{0}^{1} x^m(1 - x)^n\,dx = \int_{0}^{1} x^n(1 - x)^m\,dx\) and hence evaluate \(\int_{0}^{1} x(1 - x)^{10}\,dx\).
blocks.explanation:
A 'prove, then use' question.
On \([0, 1]\), Property IV lets us replace \(x\) by \(1 - x\); this swaps the roles of \(x\) and \(1 - x\), which is exactly the statement.
Then use it with \(m = 1\), \(n = 10\): \((1 - x)^{10}\) becomes \(x^{10}\), which is easy to integrate.
steps:
Given: \(I = \int_{0}^{1} x^m(1 - x)^n\,dx\).
To prove: \(I = \int_{0}^{1} x^n(1 - x)^m\,dx\); then evaluate \(\int_0^1 x(1 - x)^{10}\,dx\).
Method: Property IV with \(a = 0\), \(b = 1\): \(\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx = \int_0^1 f(1 - x)\,dx\).

Replace \(x\) by \(1 - x\)
\[I = \int_{0}^{1} (1 - x)^m\big(1 - (1 - x)\big)^n\,dx\]
\[= \int_{0}^{1} (1 - x)^m x^n\,dx\]
Why: Property IV; and \(1 - (1 - x) = x\).

Conclusion of the proof
\[\int_{0}^{1} x^m(1 - x)^n\,dx = \int_{0}^{1} x^n(1 - x)^m\,dx\]
Why: the order of the factors in a product does not matter.

Use it with \(m = 1\), \(n = 10\)
\[\int_{0}^{1} x(1 - x)^{10}\,dx = \int_{0}^{1} x^{10}(1 - x)\,dx\]
\[= \int_{0}^{1} (x^{10} - x^{11})\,dx\]
Why: expanding \((1 - x)^{10}\) would give 11 terms; after the swap only two terms remain.

Check by parts (without the property)
\[\int x(1 - x)^{10}dx = -\dfrac{x(1 - x)^{11}}{11}\]
\[- \dfrac{(1 - x)^{12}}{132}\]
\[\Big[\ \cdot\ \Big]_{0}^{1} = 0 - \left(-\dfrac{1}{132}\right) = \dfrac{1}{132} \;\checkmark\]
Why: by parts with \(\int (1 - x)^{10}dx = -\frac{(1 - x)^{11}}{11}\). The key prints \(\frac{1}{132}\).
